preconditions.description: The input consists of exactly two lines.
The first line contains only digits.
The number of digits in the first line does not exceed 1,000,000.
The second line contains only digits.

postconditions.description: The output is a valid integer without leading zeroes, except for the number zero itself.
The remembered substring is a substring of the restored number n.
The length of the restored number n matches the number of digits in n as specified in the input.

postconditions.expression: return_value == min([x for x in permutations(stdin.splitlines()[0][:-len(str(len(stdin.splitlines()[0]) - len(stdin.splitlines()[1]))]) if stdin.splitlines()[1] in x])
postconditions.description: The output is the smallest possible integer n that can be formed from the shuffled digits and contains the remembered substring.
